holidays.name: National Lemon Cream Pie Day
holidays.description: A day for tart, tangy lemon filling and silky cream piled into a flaky crust. It's a bright, sunny slice of dessert in the middle of late-autumn pumpkin and pecan season.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a fixture on dessert-lovers' calendars as a citrusy break from the usual holiday-season pies.
holidays.funFact: Lemon pies became popular partly because lemons and sugar were easy to store and ship. That made a bright, fresh-tasting dessert possible even in winter.

holidays.name: National Square Dancing Day
holidays.description: Grab your partner and do-si-do. This day celebrates square dancing, the lively folk dance in which four couples form a square and move together to a caller's instructions.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates a dance tradition that grew from European folk and country dances and developed into a distinctly American pastime.
holidays.funFact: Square dancing is the official state dance of more than 30 U.S. states. A caller improvises the moves, so no two dances are exactly alike.

holidays.name: Electronic Greetings Day
holidays.description: A day to send a digital greeting card, e-card, or cheerful message to someone you care about. No stamps, no mailbox trip, and no paper cuts.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that nods to the move from paper cards to digital ones. It falls just before the busy holiday-greeting season.
holidays.funFact: Online e-cards took off in the late 1990s. Sites that let you send animated greetings with a click became some of the early web's most popular destinations.
